commentary:
The story this morning is oil feeding straight into the bond market. Crude extended its rally — Brent +1.5% above $107, WTI +2.1% near $103.50 — as attacks shut a major Saudi pipeline, Houthis struck Saudi sites and Iran-Gulf talks were postponed, with WTI's prompt spread the strongest since July and Brent backwardation widening, a clear signal of physical tightness. That supply shock is turbocharging inflation fears just as the Fed meets this week: the 10-year Treasury yield punched through 5% to its highest since 2007, dragging the long bond down 0.6-0.8%, and two major Wall Street houses have switched to forecasting a hike, according to reports.

Curve pressure is concentrated at the long end — twos barely moved — a bear-steepening that says this is about inflation and term premium, not growth. That mix is toxic for risk: S&P and Nasdaq futures are off ~0.3%, Europe softer with banks lagging, and the dollar is bid across the board — every major currency is lower, with the yen down 0.5% despite Japan reportedly mulling defense spending at 3.5% of GDP, and the won off 1.4%. Precious metals are giving ground to real yields and the dollar, gold -0.9%, while copper and iron ore sag after China's steel body urged mills to cut output into weak demand.

In ags, cocoa is unwinding hard (-3.4%) and OJ ripped +5.3% on supply concerns, per reports. Watch the Fed decision, Hormuz flows and whether 5% on the 10-year holds — that level now sets the tone for everything.
